chapter: Joining Carter and Goodman in New York
title: Hammond's Cafe Society offer and Wilson's cars
summary: Hammond offered a $100-a-week steady job at Cafe Society if Wilson used his personnel; Wilson digresses on his Cadillacs and Studebaker.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So I got offered, during that time, a job at the Cafe Society downtown, which was due to John Hammond's work again, because he never liked my big band, and so he offered me a job, a steady, year round job as a band leader at the Cafe Society, but I would have to take his men, his personnel.
He wouldn't take the men out of my big band, he didn't like them -- but to his credit, he did offer us a good job.
And so I had been in debt and had lost all my money with the big bands, I took this job to
try and climb out of the debt that I owed and John Hammond offered me $100 a week in a permanent job and I knew that at least I'd have $100 a week and I could save a little money.
I knew my car was paid for, and stuff like that.
And you always had a good car.
Tell me about them cars, because you've been a car man all your life.

Yeah -- Cadillacs, LaSalles, and in those days before they used to make sports cars, and the old Big wheeling cars. Studebakers back in the old days. You could ride all over New York for a week on a gallon of gas! I remember I had a free wheeling Studebaker.
